sources.entry: Corral - Native macOS and iPhone client to follow and reply to Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and Cursor sessions with split panes. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/corral-dev/corral-apple) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Native App][Native Icon]

summary.one_liner: Corral is a native macOS and iPhone client for following and replying to coding-agent sessions (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Cursor, Pi) running on a Corral host on macOS or Linux.
keywords: watch agent progress away from desk
send instructions to ai coding assistant
summary.what_it_does: Corral lets you list sessions from Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Cursor and Pi in one place on a Mac or iPhone. On Mac you can open up to four panes side by side and switch each pane between the agent's chat view and its terminal. You can filter sessions by project and search conversation text. Replies, answers to questions, and new instructions can be sent from the Mac or an iPhone. The agents themselves run on a Corral host (macOS or Linux) that pairs with the client via a pairing code, with read-only pairing available. The README states that session traffic and notification text are end-to-end encrypted and that device keys are stored in Keychain.
use_cases: check on coding agents while away from the desk
reply to agent questions from an iPhone
run and monitor several coding sessions side by side on a Mac
search past agent conversations by project or text
pair a phone or Mac with a home or office machine running agents
self-host a relay for access from another network
how_to_run: git clone the repository, then run: xcodegen generate
Open Corral.xcodeproj in Xcode, set your own team and bundle identifiers, and build to a physical iPhone
notable: Single session list covering five coding assistants: Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Cursor and Pi
Up to four side-by-side panes on Mac, each switchable between chat and terminal view
Host runs on macOS or Linux; clients are native Apple apps
End-to-end encrypted session traffic; user runs their own relay rather than a shared hosted one
Read-only pairing option via corral remote pair --readonly
caveats: iPhone app is source-only for now; building requires Xcode, your own signing team and a physical iPhone; no App Store or TestFlight build yet
Mac app requires macOS 26+; iPhone app requires iOS 17+
No shared hosted relay; remote access from other networks requires running your own relay, and iPhone push notifications need APNs set up with your own app credentials
The host machine must stay awake for agents and remote access to keep working
